question: During the first 3 seconds of a discharge, a piston moves at a rate equal to 1 times the square of the elapsed time plus 6 times the elapsed time. The total distance the piston covers from the 0th to the 3rd second, taken as a plain number, is used as the release speed in metres per second of a projectile of mass 6000 g on the adjacent launcher. The energy the projectile carries because of its motion is recorded. The launcher fires 5 projectiles per magazine and 7 magazines are emptied in the trial, and all the energies add. The barrel is 1.2 m long. What is the total energy for the trial, in kJ?

A cart of mass 25000 g starts with zero acceleration at t = 0 s, and its acceleration grows at a rate of 2t² + 8t, in m/s³, with t in seconds, until t = 3 s. The bench is 2.0 m long. The force on the cart is what is needed to give it the acceleration reached at t = 3 s; express it in kN and take it as positive. 8 identical carts are pushed together and their forces added, after which an 8 kN retarding force and then a 29 kN braking force act against them. What is the resulting signed net force, in kN?

A container port's straddle carrier accelerates a 128000 g test block at a rate in metres per second squared equal to 2 less than the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 11x + 28 = 0. Find the force in newtons needed for one block. The carrier moves 6 blocks at once, so multiply by 6 and convert to kilonewtons. The port has 12 identical carriers, so multiply by 12. What is the total force in kN?
Calculating 4*(7 + 18) - 23 = 77 m/s^2. A 8 kg mass produces force = 616 N, scaled by 2, decreased by 11, converted to kN. A system pressure of 10 bar is noted. What is the final force in kN?

A cannery receives 132 lids of one type and 359 of another, and it packs them into identical cases using the largest case size that divides both counts exactly. A pusher then drives a tray of mass 40000 g at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, equal to 5 times that case size. The line's log subtracts 8 N for the rail friction and adds 24 N for the return-spring preload. The line's steriliser is rated at 12 kW. Ten identical pushers work the floor, and the log reports 10 times the single-pusher figure. What does the log report, in N?

A depot holds 89 crates on one dock and 328 on another, and the supervisor works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. That number is, in metres per second squared, the acceleration his tug applies to a load of 66 kg. The control system works out the force needed to move the load and expresses it in kilonewtons. It multiplies the converted figure by 9 for the 9 tugs in the depot, and then by 7 for the 7 days in the week. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the control system report?

Solving x^2 - 3x + 2 = 0 for the larger root is 2 m/s, scaled by 8 to get 16. A 21 kg mass has kinetic energy decreased by 3, decreased by 27, scaled by 8. A reference is 100 m/s. What is the final energy in joules?

A crane hire firm's fleet figure is 9 times a site's total, expressed in kilonewtons. A site's total is the frame force plus 13 kN for the outrigger pads. A frame carries 8 identical hoists pulling together, and one hoist drives a load of mass 46000 g. That load's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is numerically equal to the number of different pairs that can be chosen from the frame's 12 anchor eyes, taking 2 at a time. The firm's yard fence runs 90 m. What is the firm's fleet figure, in kN?

The second derivative of f(x) = 4x^3 + 6x^2 at x=1 is 20. A 59 kg object (stated as 59000 grams) at this develops kinetic energy. After converting to kJ, adding 14, and subtracting 26, what is the final energy in kilojoules?

A 113 000 g cargo pod is accelerated along a launch rail at a rate, in m/s², equal to the rate at which the slope of the curve y = 2x³ + 4x² is itself changing at x = 2. The rail's motor must also overcome 24 N of guide friction and 10 N of air drag. The motor's total force is expressed in kilonewtons, and a 28 kN safety margin is added for the rating. What is the rating, in kN?

A ferry terminal is rating a linkspan actuator. The span's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying a^2 - 9a + 20 = 0. The moving span has a mass of 65 kg, and the control room is at 19 degrees C. The actuator supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. A counterweight chain adds 19 N to the actuator's load, and a guide roller then relieves 12 N. The terminal has 8 identical linkspans. What total load, in N, do the linkspans carry?
The second derivative of 3x^3 + 2x^2 at x = 4 is 76 m/s. A 37 kg mass has kinetic energy converted to kJ, scaled by 7, decreased by 21. A power is 100 W. What is the final energy in kJ?

On a lab test bench, two speed values, in m/s, sum to 10 and multiply to 16; the larger is kept as the speed of a slider whose mass is stated as 37000 grams. The slider's kinetic energy is scaled by a factor of 6, scaled again by 5, then reduced by 23 J, and finally reduced once more by 4 J. What is the final energy, in joules?

An oscillation equation f(x) = 2x³ - 5x² has its second time derivative evaluated at x = 1. This second derivative becomes the velocity in m/s for a 57 kg oscillating element. The kinetic energy is calculated. The energy converts from joules to kilojoules. Adding 23 kJ for stored energy increases it. Subtracting 26 kJ for dissipated energy decreases it. What is the final kinetic energy in kJ? (The oscillation amplitude is 5 cm, which is not used.)

At a model-rocket sled test track, a sled's position, in meters, follows s(t) = 5t^3 - 3t^2, where t is the time in seconds after launch. Engineers need how sharply the sled's motion is changing at t = 2 seconds. That value applies as the speed, in meters per second, of a sled with a mass of 18,000 grams. (The sled's guide rail is 6.5 meters long, a fact that plays no role here.) Find the energy this sled carries at that speed, in joules, then add 15 to that number. Convert what results into kilojoules, and then multiply the result by 12. What is the final number, in kilojoules?

A logger shows the rate at which a gearbox shaft's acceleration is changing, r(t) = t² + 3t (meters per second cubed), between t = 0 s and t = 1 s since startup; the net increase in acceleration this produces is tripled for a three-shaft gearbox, giving the true acceleration of a 68,000 gram shaft. Find the resulting force, subtract 10 newtons for a bearing-friction correction, and convert the total to kilonewtons. A separate flow gauge nearby reads 3 liters per second, unrelated to this calculation. What is the final force, in kilonewtons?

A vibration test platform at x = 3 stores energy from a 31 kg mass. The second derivative of x³ + 3x² yields 30 m/s² at that point, producing kinetic energy, increased by 5 J for pre-stress, amplified 12 times through isolation stages, 9 more times through damping multipliers, then converted to kJ. A humidity sensor reads 48% but is unused. What is the total isolation energy in kJ?

The integral from 0 to 1 of (2x^2 + 3x) dx gives velocity for 19 kg mass kinetic energy. After subtracting 10 and adding 13, the energy is converted to kJ and scaled by 7. What is the final energy in kJ?
GCD(301, 28) = 7. With 37 kg, energy = 0.5 × 37 × 7² = 907.5 J, times 5, convert to 4.5375 kJ, times 6, minus 20. The link capacity is 1 Gbps. What is the final energy in kJ?

A launcher takes the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 14x + 48 = 0 and reads it as a release speed in metres per second. A dart of mass 33000 g is released at that speed along a level rail, and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules. The rig fires 7 darts in a magazine and their energies add, and 7 identical magazines are emptied in the trial with those energies adding too. What is the trial total, in kJ?
The calculation 4*(8+7) = 60 gives velocity for 34 kg kinetic energy, reduced by 23 J. Energy is converted to kJ and increased by 7 kJ. What is the final energy in kJ?

A ski-lift maintenance shop tests a carrier on a short rail. The carrier's speed, in metres per second, is the area under the curve 1*x^2 + 0*x between x = 2 and x = 3, where x is the drive-lever index. The carrier has a mass of 31000 g, and the energy it carries by virtue of that motion is multiplied by the 11 carriers on the rail. A charged latch then adds 15 J to that total, and the result is expressed in kilojoules. The shop runs 2 identical rails. What total energy, in kJ, do the rails hold?

A moving system's velocity is the smaller root of x squared minus 3 times x plus 2 equals zero. A 33-kilogram component at this velocity develops kinetic energy as half mass times velocity squared. Convert from Joules to kilojoules. Subtract 13 kilojoules, multiply by 10, and multiply by 9 to find the performance metric. A surface area of 15 square metres was involved but does not affect the energy. What is the performance metric in kilojoules?

The final step of this test rig's calculation always subtracts 26 from the kilonewton reading right before it's logged — keep that in mind. A test fixture on a factory bench has a mass of 99 kilograms. A technician takes 9 units, adds 11 units, and multiplies the sum by 3, then adds 7 to the result — this final number is the fixture's acceleration, in meters per second squared. Using that acceleration and the fixture's mass, a certain force is found. That force, in newtons, is converted into kilonewtons, and finally, exactly as noted at the start, 26 is subtracted. What is the resulting force, in kilonewtons?

Integrate 5x² + 4x from 0 to 2. A system with mass 3 kilograms operates at this velocity. Calculate kinetic energy. Convert to kiloJoules. Scale by 9. Scale by 6. Add 26. What is the final energy in kiloJoules?
